chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about nosebleed and cupping, and every flowing blood, so he said: There is no ablution (wudu) in this. Rather, the ablution is from your two lower ends which Allah, the Exalted, has favored with upon you.

key_terms.طَرَفَيْكَ: Your two ends (referring to the two exit points of impurity)

ai.seo_question: Does a nosebleed break wudu or require ghusl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that flowing blood from the nose or cupping does not invalidate wudu, reinforcing the Shia juristic view that wudu is primarily triggered by the exit of waste from the two lower extremities (urethra and anus). This distinction highlights the precision in Shia fiqh regarding minor impurity (hadath al-asghar) versus other bodily discharges, ensuring that ritual purity is maintained without unnecessary repetition of ablution.
